vocabulary.definition: A Git commit records a snapshot reference plus metadata and parent relationships, forming history as a graph of commit objects.
A Git commit records a project state and references its parent commit or commits, forming commit history.
A Git branch is a named line of development represented by a reference that normally advances as new commits are created.
HEAD identifies the commit currently checked out, usually indirectly through the current branch reference.
git merge incorporates changes from named commits into the current branch and may create a merge commit when histories require it.
git rebase replays selected commits on top of another base and updates the branch to the replayed history.

vocabulary.definition: A Git commit records a snapshot reference plus metadata and parent relationships, forming history as a graph of commit objects.
A Git commit records a project state and references its parent commit or commits, forming commit history.
A Git branch is a named line of development represented by a reference that normally advances as new commits are created.
HEAD identifies the commit currently checked out, usually indirectly through the current branch reference.
git merge incorporates changes from named commits into the current branch and may create a merge commit when histories require it.
git rebase replays selected commits on top of another base and updates the branch to the replayed history.
